mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,400K signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1400 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS decreases by > 100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for four consecutive months signals accelerating inflation, which prompts central bank tightening and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the mortgage interest rate spread (implied from RSAFS) below 3% for two months signals an easing monetary environment, which boosts borrowing and investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND RSAFS implied rate < 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
